reading.body:
SoftBank Group's four granted US patents since 2001 include solar panel adjustment and crop management, not AI compute or data center infrastructure.

The patent record is thin and skewed. Four grants over roughly 25 years, with the two most recent titled only "System," gives no evidence of an intellectual property position in chips, cooling, or power delivery. The two titled patents point at energy and agriculture, which are adjacent to the grid constraint on AI but do not address it directly.

The company's own website frames it around the AI revolution and the possibilities AI brings, and it is a holding company with group companies rather than an operator. That structure means any exposure to AI compute runs through its portfolio, and the data here contains no portfolio, no products, and no lawsuits. Nothing in this record shows what SoftBank owns, builds, or powers.

What the data does not cover is the substance: no investment list, no subsidiary detail, no financials, no filings. The patent count is a narrow signal drawn from one applicant phrase in USPTO grants, and it should not be read as a measure of the company's role in AI infrastructure.
